objective: Improve public COLA label evidence extraction while keeping deterministic validation as the final authority.

splitting_policy.why: Images from the same COLA record must not appear in both train and validation/test.

models.name: PaddleOCR PP-OCR
models.use_when: We need one fast full-image OCR pass with text geometry preserved for field extraction.
models.expected_value: Reads arbitrary label layouts and supplies line/token boxes for LayoutLMv3 evidence extraction.
models.risk: Requires the most annotation discipline and package/runtime management.

models.name: LayoutLMv3 token classifier
models.use_when: PaddleOCR has produced full-image text tokens and bounding boxes.
models.expected_value: Learns which source OCR tokens correspond to brand, class/type, ABV, net contents, producer, country, and government warning fields.
models.risk: Only extracts spans from OCR output; it cannot recover text PaddleOCR failed to read. Synthetic labels must not contaminate final test metrics.

models.name: EasyOCR
models.role: backend escalation and fast curation detector
models.use_when: Default detector is good enough but recognition fails on stylized label text.
models.expected_value: Already works well locally and can be plugged into the worker path.
models.risk: Custom recognition training is less turnkey than PaddleOCR and does not solve layout by itself.

models.name: Tesseract LSTM
models.role: browser/CPU baseline and specialty recognizer candidate
models.use_when: We have clean line crops and want small CPU-side improvements for a narrow alphabet/style.
models.expected_value: Small deploy footprint and browser-adjacent baseline.
models.risk: Training is ground-truth-file heavy and not a field/crop detector.

models.name: CLIP or SigLIP region ranker
models.use_when: We need to choose which detected text blob is likely ABV, warning, brand, producer, etc.
models.expected_value: Can learn label-layout semantics and reduce OCR passes.
models.risk: Not safe for exact text or numeric validation; must feed OCR/validators.

models.name: docTR
models.use_when: PaddleOCR integration cost is high or we want a PyTorch-native OCR benchmark.
models.expected_value: Good research/benchmark option with deep-learning OCR pieces.
models.risk: Less aligned with current worker scheduler than EasyOCR/PaddleOCR.

promotion_rule: Only promote a trained model when it improves validation-set field recall without increasing false passes on the untouched test set.
